This script makes Tables 1 and 2 (characteristics and immunosuppression by vital status 6 months after admission) and the odds-ratio table, following plan [§8](analysis-plan.qmd#8-statistical-analysis) and the disclosure rules in [§10](analysis-plan.qmd#10-disclosure-control). The tables are written to `tables/`, which is not in the repository; they appear on this site only after USRDS review clears them.

::: {.Rcode title="Source code"}
The full R script is available at:

-   [`R/report_tables.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Fiorica-cryptoccoccus-analysis/blob/main/R/report_tables.R)

This R script file is itself reliant on the following helper files:

-   [`R/setup.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Fiorica-cryptoccoccus-analysis/blob/main/R/setup.R)
-   [`R/functions.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Fiorica-cryptoccoccus-analysis/blob/main/R/functions.R)
-   [`R/create_outcomes.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Fiorica-cryptoccoccus-analysis/blob/main/R/create_outcomes.R)
-   [`R/fit_models.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Fiorica-cryptoccoccus-analysis/blob/main/R/fit_models.R)

The code sections below are imported directly from the script when this page is rendered.
:::

## Descriptive tables

One function makes both descriptive tables. Continuous variables are shown as mean (SD), time since transplant as median (IQR), and everything else as a count and percentage, with the number unknown always shown. Continuous variables are compared with Student's t test; categorical ones with the chi-squared test, or Fisher's exact test when an expected count is under 5.

Before the table is shown, every count from 1 to 10 is hidden, along with any other count that would let it be worked out by subtraction, and the P value of that variable is removed (`flag_small_cells()` and `suppress_table_body()` on the [Functions](functions.qmd) page).

## Odds ratios

Each variable alone, and the final model after backward elimination, side by side. The P value shown for each variable is the single joint test the selection used, so a variable with several categories has one P value, not one per category.
